result.authors: ['Ying Zhao', ' Hao Lin', ' Wei Chen', ' Chunxia Wang', ' Qiang Li']
result.keywords: This study examines a hybrid geospatial framework for jointly identifying terrain-like urban path positions from high-resolution DEM surfaces and aligning dense GPS trajectories to the resulting spatial units. To improve robustness in complex built environments, the proposed method integrates local attribute analysis and regional context cues, combining rule-based segmentation, supervised classification, and object-oriented refinement within a hierarchical workflow. A two-tier position definition is introduced to distinguish intersection-adjacent zones from general corridor segments, enabling more consistent mapping between topographic structure and movement traces. Experiments on an urban test area using 2 m DEM data and high-frequency GPS samples demonstrate improved positional consistency, stronger inter-class separation, and reduced intra-class variation compared with single-method baselines. The results suggest that multimodal classification can capture both geometric terrain characteristics and trajectory behavior patterns, supporting applications in urban mobility analysis, landform interpretation, and map matching.
result.title: Multimodal Path-Position Classification for High-Resolution Urban DEM and Trajectory Alignment
